questions.q: Where do sensitivity labels in Power BI actually come from?
options: They are unique to Power BI and unrelated to any other Microsoft product
Microsoft Purview Information Protection — the same labeling system used across Word, Excel, and Outlook
They are generated automatically from a dataset's refresh history
They come from the workspace's Admin role settings
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels are a Microsoft Purview Information Protection feature extended into Power BI, using the organization's own existing label taxonomy, not a Power BI-specific system.

questions.q: What has to happen before sensitivity labels appear in Power BI at all?
options: Every semantic model must first be certified
A tenant admin has to enable sensitivity labels for Power BI
Every user must individually request access to labeling
A gateway connection must be configured
questions.explain: Sensitivity labels don't appear in Power BI until a tenant admin enables the feature; once enabled, the organization's existing label taxonomy becomes available on Power BI content.

questions.q: Where does an applied sensitivity label show in Power BI Desktop?
options: Only in a separate admin portal, never inside Desktop itself
In the status bar at the bottom of the window
It is hidden from the report author entirely
Only after the report is published to the service
questions.explain: Once applied via the Sensitivity control on the Home ribbon, the label shows directly in Desktop's status bar, and it travels with the file when it's published.

questions.q: Can a report and the semantic model it's built from carry different sensitivity labels?
options: No — labels must always match exactly across related items or publishing fails
Yes — each item can carry its own label, though a mismatch is usually worth investigating
No — only semantic models can have sensitivity labels, never reports
Yes, but only if the tenant has disabled mandatory labeling
questions.explain: Reports, semantic models, dataflows, and dashboards can each carry their own label independently — they don't have to match, but a mismatch across closely related items is a signal something may have been missed.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a sensitivity label does NOT automatically guarantee?
options: That the label is visible in the status bar
That the label travels with exports like Excel or PDF
That technical enforcement, such as encryption and content marking, is always applied
That the label can be set on a dashboard
questions.explain: Both service screenshots carry the warning that some label settings, like encryption and content marking, are not enforced in Power BI. A label always classifies, but whether it also enforces real protection depends on the tenant's label policy configuration.
